text:
Kris Letang has played 1,259 games for Pittsburgh, won three Stanley Cups and a Masterton Trophy, and now finds his name in a different kind of headline. The New York Times asked where Crosby, Malkin and Letang go from here with the Penguins' season spiraling, and NHL Trade Rumors relayed a report that the team can't find a trade market for him. Pittsburgh lost eight of the ten games in his recent log.

On the ice, he is holding up better than the standings. He still plays 20:07 a night, the Penguins get 55% of the 5-on-5 chance quality with him out there, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.4 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 93rd percentile among defensemen. What's missing is finishing and timing. He has 1 goal on 44 shots, and by our wins-added measure (how much his goals swung win chances) he ranks 565th of 567 skaters. Our numbers project about 34 points. The bigger question is where he plays them.
headline: Kris Letang, 39, inside a Penguins season going sideways
